data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Titus means 'honoring' or 'grace'. In the New Testament, Titus was a Greek Christian and a companion of Paul. He was later entrusted with the task of organizing and overseeing the Christian communities in Crete.

Numerous churches, organizations, and institutions have taken on the name Titus in honor of the Apostle and the spiritual leadership he exemplified.

The name serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, faith, and leadership in the Christian faith. Those named Titus are encouraged to embody Titus's qualities as they strive to grow in their own spiritual journeys and serve their communities in love and grace.

historical_references.context: Paul mentions Titus in several of his letters, describing him as a trusted colleague and a pastor overseeing various Christian communities.
